paragraphs.title: The Tabernacle Curtains and Their Joining

easy.question: How many curtains were Moses commanded to make for the Tabernacle?
easy.explanation: The first verse says, “Ten curtains.”

easy.question: What were the dimensions of each curtain?
easy.explanation: Each curtain was twenty-eight cubits long and four cubits wide.

easy.question: What was made on the curtains?
easy.explanation: The verse says that the curtains were made with cherubim in skillful work.

medium.question: How were the ten curtains arranged before they were joined?
answers: Five curtains were joined into one group and five into another
Each curtain was attached to a separate pillar
All ten curtains were joined together at once
medium.explanation: The verses describe two groups, each consisting of five joined curtains.

medium.question: What was the purpose of the blue loops along the curtain edges?
answers: They were loops for joining the curtains
medium.explanation: The loops were made along the curtain edges so the two groups could be fastened together.

medium.question: What was the result of joining the curtains with the gold clasps?
answers: The curtains received a new color
medium.explanation: The verse concludes, “and it shall be one tabernacle.”

challenge.question: What was made after the loops were prepared along the curtain edges?
answers: Fifty gold clasps for joining them
All the curtains were measured again
challenge.explanation: After commanding the loops, the text says, “And thou shalt make fifty taches of gold.”

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “one measure” for all the curtains?
answers: Only five curtains were the same size
All the curtains had equal dimensions
The curtains had different sizes according to their colors
challenge.explanation: The phrase indicates that every curtain had the same measurements.

challenge.question: Why were the loops placed opposite one another?
answers: So each curtain would have a different color
To separate the two groups of curtains
To allow the two groups to be joined precisely
challenge.explanation: Matching loops along the edges of the two groups allowed them to be joined with clasps and become one Tabernacle.

questions.question: What was made after the loops were prepared along the curtain edges?
answers: Fifty gold clasps for joining them
All the curtains were measured again
questions.explanation: After commanding the loops, the text says, “And thou shalt make fifty taches of gold.”

questions.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “one measure” for all the curtains?
answers: Only five curtains were the same size
All the curtains had equal dimensions
The curtains had different sizes according to their colors
questions.explanation: The phrase indicates that every curtain had the same measurements.

questions.question: Why were the loops placed opposite one another?
answers: So each curtain would have a different color
To separate the two groups of curtains
To allow the two groups to be joined precisely
questions.explanation: Matching loops along the edges of the two groups allowed them to be joined with clasps and become one Tabernacle.

paragraphs.title: The Goats’ Hair Curtains and the Coverings

easy.question: What were the curtains intended as a tent over the Tabernacle made of?
easy.explanation: Verse 7 says, “You shall make curtains of goats’ hair.”

easy.question: What was the length of each curtain?
easy.explanation: Verse 8 says that each curtain was thirty cubits long.

easy.question: What was the upper covering of the tent?
easy.explanation: Verse 14 says that a covering of badgers’ skins was placed above.

medium.question: What was the purpose of the clasps and loops?
answers: To join the tent into one unit
medium.explanation: The clasps were placed in the loops to join the curtains, making the tent one.

medium.question: In the phrase “the remnant that remaineth,” what does “remnant” mean?
answers: The extra portion that extends beyond its proper place
medium.explanation: The context explains that the remnant was the extra part of the curtains that extended beyond the tent.

medium.question: How were the curtains joined before the tent became one?
answers: All the curtains were joined at once
They were all folded in half
Five curtains were joined separately and six separately
medium.explanation: The text commands that five curtains be joined separately and six separately, and then that the groups be joined together.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from making fifty loops on each joining edge and fifty copper clasps?
answers: There were fifty joining points between the two groups
Each curtain was made of fifty pieces
There were fifty curtains in each group
challenge.explanation: The equal number of loops and clasps shows that they were meant to connect along the edges of the two groups.

challenge.question: Which curtain was to be folded toward the front of the tent?
challenge.explanation: Verse 9 explicitly says, “and shalt double the sixth curtain in the forefront of the tabernacle.”

challenge.question: Why was an extra cubit left on each side along the length of the tent curtains?
answers: To cover the sides of the Tabernacle
challenge.explanation: Verse 13 explains that the extra portion on both sides would hang over the sides of the Tabernacle to cover it.

questions.question: What can be inferred from making fifty loops on each joining edge and fifty copper clasps?
answers: There were fifty joining points between the two groups
Each curtain was made of fifty pieces
There were fifty curtains in each group
questions.explanation: The equal number of loops and clasps shows that they were meant to connect along the edges of the two groups.

questions.question: Which curtain was to be folded toward the front of the tent?
questions.explanation: Verse 9 explicitly says, “and shalt double the sixth curtain in the forefront of the tabernacle.”

questions.question: Why was an extra cubit left on each side along the length of the tent curtains?
answers: To cover the sides of the Tabernacle
questions.explanation: Verse 13 explains that the extra portion on both sides would hang over the sides of the Tabernacle to cover it.

paragraphs.title: The Boards of the Tabernacle and the Silver Sockets

easy.question: What kind of wood was used for the boards of the Tabernacle?
easy.explanation: Verse 15 says that the boards were to be made of shittim wood.

easy.question: What was the length of each board?
easy.explanation: Verse 16 says, “Ten cubits shall be the length of a board.”

easy.question: How many boards were on the west side of the Tabernacle, including the corner boards?
easy.explanation: The west side had six boards plus two corner boards, making eight in all.

medium.question: Why were forty silver sockets needed beneath the twenty boards on the south side?
answers: Because each board had two sockets
Because each board had one socket
Because each board had four sockets
medium.explanation: The text specifies two sockets for each board, so twenty boards required forty sockets.

medium.question: In the phrase “for the sides of the Tabernacle westward,” what does “sides” refer to?
answers: The rear or far end of the Tabernacle
The north side of the Tabernacle
medium.explanation: The context shows that this refers to the rear, western end of the Tabernacle.

medium.question: What did the south and north sides of the Tabernacle have in common?
answers: Both had twenty boards and forty silver sockets
medium.explanation: Both the south and north sides had twenty boards and forty silver sockets.

challenge.question: How is the number eight obtained for the boards on the west side?
answers: Six boards plus two corner boards
challenge.explanation: Verses 22–23 mention six western boards and two additional boards for the corners.

challenge.question: What does the description “joined together beneath... joined together above” teach about the corner boards?
answers: They were shorter than the other boards
They were fitted and joined together from bottom to top
They were placed only above the Tabernacle
challenge.explanation: The description emphasizes that the two corner boards were joined together along their entire height.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the boards’ dimensions and the phrase “standing up”?
answers: They were short beams for the floor
They were upright boards forming the walls of the Tabernacle
challenge.explanation: Their great height and the phrase “standing up” show that they stood upright to form the Tabernacle walls.

questions.question: How is the number eight obtained for the boards on the west side?
answers: Six boards plus two corner boards
questions.explanation: Verses 22–23 mention six western boards and two additional boards for the corners.

questions.question: What does the description “joined together beneath... joined together above” teach about the corner boards?
answers: They were shorter than the other boards
They were fitted and joined together from bottom to top
They were placed only above the Tabernacle
questions.explanation: The description emphasizes that the two corner boards were joined together along their entire height.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the boards’ dimensions and the phrase “standing up”?
answers: They were short beams for the floor
They were upright boards forming the walls of the Tabernacle
questions.explanation: Their great height and the phrase “standing up” show that they stood upright to form the Tabernacle walls.

paragraphs.title: The Bars and the Gold Covering

easy.question: What kind of wood was to be used for the bars?
easy.explanation: The verse explicitly says, “bars of shittim wood.”

easy.question: How many bars were intended for each side of the Tabernacle?
easy.explanation: The verses repeatedly say that each side was to have five bars.

easy.question: With what were the boards and bars to be covered?
easy.explanation: Verse 29 says to overlay the boards and the bars with gold.

medium.question: What was special about the middle bar compared with the other bars?
answers: It reached from end to end through the boards
It was found only on the east side
medium.explanation: The verse emphasizes that the middle bar passed through the boards from end to end.

medium.question: What does “the sides westward” mean in this passage?
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the western, rear side of the Tabernacle.

medium.question: What was done after the command to make the bars?
answers: The boards and bars were covered with gold
medium.explanation: The next verse commands that the boards, rings, and bars be overlaid with gold.

challenge.question: What was the purpose of the gold rings made for the boards?
answers: They served as holders for the bars
They decorated the entrance of the Tabernacle
challenge.explanation: The verse says that the rings were to be places for the bars, where the bars could pass through and be held.

challenge.question: According to the passage, how many bars were mentioned for the three sides?
challenge.explanation: There were five bars for one side, five for the other, and five for the western side: fifteen altogether.

challenge.question: Which detail especially distinguishes the middle bar?
answers: Only it was covered with gold
Only it was made of shittim wood
It passed through the boards from end to end
challenge.explanation: Although all the bars were covered with gold, only the middle bar is specifically said to pass through the boards from end to end.

questions.question: What was the purpose of the gold rings made for the boards?
answers: They served as holders for the bars
They decorated the entrance of the Tabernacle
questions.explanation: The verse says that the rings were to be places for the bars, where the bars could pass through and be held.

questions.question: According to the passage, how many bars were mentioned for the three sides?
questions.explanation: There were five bars for one side, five for the other, and five for the western side: fifteen altogether.

questions.question: Which detail especially distinguishes the middle bar?
answers: Only it was covered with gold
Only it was made of shittim wood
It passed through the boards from end to end
questions.explanation: Although all the bars were covered with gold, only the middle bar is specifically said to pass through the boards from end to end.

paragraphs.title: Setting Up the Tabernacle According to the Pattern

easy.question: What was Moses commanded to set up?
easy.explanation: The verse commands, “Thou shalt rear up the tabernacle.”

easy.question: Where did the LORD show Moses the model?
easy.explanation: The verse ends with, “which was shewed thee in the mount.”

easy.question: How was the Tabernacle to be set up?
easy.explanation: The verse commands that it be erected according to the pattern shown to Moses.

medium.question: Why did Moses have to set up the Tabernacle according to its pattern?
answers: He had to follow the model shown to him
He had to change the model
The Tabernacle had no particular arrangement
medium.explanation: The verse connects the required arrangement with what the LORD showed Moses on the mountain.

medium.question: In the phrase “according to the fashion thereof,” what does “fashion” mean?
answers: According to its prescribed form and arrangement
At the time of a trial
medium.explanation: In this context, “fashion” means the proper pattern and arrangement shown to Moses.

medium.question: Which relationship between the two parts of the verse is correct?
answers: The setup had to match what the LORD showed on the mountain
The mountain vision came after the Tabernacle was built
The Tabernacle was set up without reference to the mountain vision
medium.explanation: The verse teaches that the model shown on the mountain was the basis for setting up the Tabernacle.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the command to set up the Tabernacle “according to the fashion thereof”?
answers: Moses was not permitted to alter the pattern he received
Moses could choose any pattern he wished
The Tabernacle was meant to be different each time
challenge.explanation: The command required Moses to follow the model shown to him, leaving no room for personal changes.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “which was shewed thee in the mount” refer to?
answers: The specific model shown to Moses
challenge.explanation: The phrase refers to the Tabernacle pattern that the LORD showed Moses on the mountain.

challenge.question: Which wording emphasizes that the command concerned a specific model rather than only a general idea?
challenge.explanation: These words point to a particular model that had been shown to Moses.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the command to set up the Tabernacle “according to the fashion thereof”?
answers: Moses was not permitted to alter the pattern he received
Moses could choose any pattern he wished
The Tabernacle was meant to be different each time
questions.explanation: The command required Moses to follow the model shown to him, leaving no room for personal changes.

questions.question: What does the phrase “which was shewed thee in the mount” refer to?
answers: The specific model shown to Moses
questions.explanation: The phrase refers to the Tabernacle pattern that the LORD showed Moses on the mountain.

questions.question: Which wording emphasizes that the command concerned a specific model rather than only a general idea?
questions.explanation: These words point to a particular model that had been shown to Moses.

easy.question: What were they commanded to make in this verse?
easy.explanation: The verse begins, “And thou shalt make a vail.”

easy.question: Which of these appears in the list of materials for the veil?
easy.explanation: Blue is listed among the colors and materials of the veil.

easy.question: What was designed or woven into the veil?
easy.explanation: The verse says that the veil was to be made with cherubim.

medium.question: What can be understood from the phrase “of cunning work”?
answers: The veil was an artistic and skillfully made work
The veil was plain and undecorated
The veil was made only of wood
medium.explanation: The phrase describes skilled, artistic workmanship rather than plain fabric.

medium.question: What is a veil in the context of “thou shalt make a vail”?
answers: A tool for lighting a fire
A curtain or screen separating areas
medium.explanation: The context presents it as a decorated fabric curtain separating parts of the Tabernacle.

medium.question: Which description correctly combines the materials and workmanship?
answers: A plain white veil without decoration
A metal veil made by casting
A veil of various fabrics and colors, skillfully made with cherubim
medium.explanation: The verse mentions blue, purple, scarlet, fine twined linen, skilled work, and cherubim.

challenge.question: What does the word “cherubim” add to the description of the veil?
answers: It included a sacred design or image of significant heavenly beings
It was used for eating sacrifices
challenge.explanation: “Cherubim” describes a sacred design or decoration, not a material.

challenge.question: Why should “cunning work” not be understood as meaning that the veil merely made people think?
answers: Because “cunning” refers here to a color
Because the phrase describes planned, skilled craftsmanship
Because the verse speaks only about the veil’s dimensions
challenge.explanation: In this context, “cunning work” means carefully planned and skillful artistic workmanship.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that the veil was not plain, single-colored fabric?
answers: The variety of colors, threads, and cherubim
challenge.explanation: The list of colors and materials, together with the cherubim and skilled work, shows that the veil was richly decorated.

questions.question: What does the word “cherubim” add to the description of the veil?
answers: It included a sacred design or image of significant heavenly beings
It was used for eating sacrifices
questions.explanation: “Cherubim” describes a sacred design or decoration, not a material.

questions.question: Why should “cunning work” not be understood as meaning that the veil merely made people think?
answers: Because “cunning” refers here to a color
Because the phrase describes planned, skilled craftsmanship
Because the verse speaks only about the veil’s dimensions
questions.explanation: In this context, “cunning work” means carefully planned and skillful artistic workmanship.

questions.question: Which detail shows that the veil was not plain, single-colored fabric?
answers: The variety of colors, threads, and cherubim
questions.explanation: The list of colors and materials, together with the cherubim and skilled work, shows that the veil was richly decorated.

paragraphs.title: The Pillars and Sockets of the Veil

easy.question: How many pillars supported the veil?
easy.explanation: The verse says, “upon four pillars of shittim wood.”

easy.question: What covered the pillars?
easy.explanation: The verse says that the pillars were overlaid with gold.

easy.question: What were the sockets made of?
easy.explanation: The verse ends with “four sockets of silver.”

medium.question: What material is mentioned both for the pillars’ covering and their hooks?
medium.explanation: The pillars were overlaid with gold, and their hooks were also made of gold.

medium.question: In the phrase “four sockets of silver,” what are sockets?
medium.explanation: Sockets were the bases into which the pillars were set.

medium.question: Which combination correctly describes the structure?
answers: Four pillars and two silver sockets
Two pillars and four gold sockets
Four pillars and four silver sockets
medium.explanation: The verse mentions four pillars and four silver sockets.

challenge.question: Which of the following was not made of or covered with gold according to the verse?
challenge.explanation: The sockets were silver, while the pillars were covered with gold and the hooks were gold.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the equal number of pillars and sockets?
answers: All the sockets were made of wood
Each pillar had a corresponding base
challenge.explanation: The verse mentions four pillars and four sockets, suggesting one base for each pillar.

challenge.question: What does the pronoun in “their hooks” refer to?
challenge.explanation: The pronoun refers to the pillars mentioned earlier, so these were the pillars’ hooks.

questions.question: Which of the following was not made of or covered with gold according to the verse?
questions.explanation: The sockets were silver, while the pillars were covered with gold and the hooks were gold.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the equal number of pillars and sockets?
answers: All the sockets were made of wood
Each pillar had a corresponding base
questions.explanation: The verse mentions four pillars and four sockets, suggesting one base for each pillar.

questions.question: What does the pronoun in “their hooks” refer to?
questions.explanation: The pronoun refers to the pillars mentioned earlier, so these were the pillars’ hooks.

paragraphs.title: The Veil and the Ark of the Testimony

easy.question: What was to be placed under the clasps?
easy.explanation: The verse commands, “Thou shalt hang up the vail under the taches.”

easy.question: What was inside the Most Holy Place?
easy.explanation: The text says that the Ark of the Testimony was brought inside the veil, into the Most Holy Place.

easy.question: What was to be placed on the Ark of the Testimony?
easy.explanation: Verse 34 says, “Thou shalt put the mercy seat upon the ark of the testimony.”

medium.question: What was the function of the veil?
answers: To separate the Holy Place from the Most Holy
medium.explanation: The veil divided the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place.

medium.question: What is the mercy seat in the phrase “upon the ark of the testimony”?
answers: The upper cover of the Ark
medium.explanation: The context shows that the mercy seat was the cover or upper panel placed on the Ark.

medium.question: What order of actions is described in these verses?
answers: Hang the veil, bring the Ark behind it, then place the mercy seat on the Ark
Place the mercy seat, remove the veil, then bring in the Ark
Bring in the Ark, remove it from the Tabernacle, then hang the veil
medium.explanation: The passage first describes hanging the veil, then bringing the Ark behind it, and finally placing the mercy seat on the Ark.

challenge.question: What follows from the statement that the Ark was “within the vail”?
answers: The Ark was in front of the veil
The Ark was outside the Tabernacle
The Ark was on the inner side of the veil, in the Most Holy Place
challenge.explanation: “Within the veil” means on its inner side, in the Most Holy Place.

challenge.question: What is the relationship between the mercy seat and the Ark in these verses?
answers: The mercy seat was placed on the Ark, and both were in the Most Holy Place
The mercy seat separated the Ark from the Most Holy Place
The mercy seat was in the Holy Place while the Ark was in the Most Holy
challenge.explanation: The verse says that the mercy seat was placed on the Ark, which was in the Most Holy Place.

challenge.question: What important detail about the veil might be overlooked?
answers: It covered the Ark of the Testimony
It also served as a partition between two holy areas
It was above the mercy seat
challenge.explanation: The veil was not the Ark’s cover; it separated the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place, while the mercy seat rested on the Ark.

questions.question: What follows from the statement that the Ark was “within the vail”?
answers: The Ark was in front of the veil
The Ark was outside the Tabernacle
The Ark was on the inner side of the veil, in the Most Holy Place
questions.explanation: “Within the veil” means on its inner side, in the Most Holy Place.

questions.question: What is the relationship between the mercy seat and the Ark in these verses?
answers: The mercy seat was placed on the Ark, and both were in the Most Holy Place
The mercy seat separated the Ark from the Most Holy Place
The mercy seat was in the Holy Place while the Ark was in the Most Holy
questions.explanation: The verse says that the mercy seat was placed on the Ark, which was in the Most Holy Place.

questions.question: What important detail about the veil might be overlooked?
answers: It covered the Ark of the Testimony
It also served as a partition between two holy areas
It was above the mercy seat
questions.explanation: The veil was not the Ark’s cover; it separated the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place, while the mercy seat rested on the Ark.

paragraphs.title: The Arrangement of the Table and the Lampstand

easy.question: Where was the table to be placed?
easy.explanation: The verse commands that the table be placed outside the veil.

easy.question: What was placed opposite the table?
easy.explanation: The verse says, “the candlestick over against the table.”

easy.question: On which side of the Tabernacle was the table placed?
easy.explanation: The verse says that the table was placed on the north side.

medium.question: How were the table and lampstand positioned relative to each other?
answers: The lampstand was beneath the table
The lampstand was opposite the table
The lampstand was behind the table
medium.explanation: The phrase “over against” means that the lampstand stood opposite the table.

medium.question: In the phrase “over against the table,” what does “over against” mean?
medium.explanation: The phrase means that the lampstand was opposite or facing the table.

medium.question: Why are the south and north directions mentioned?
answers: To establish the locations of the furnishings
To indicate the time of construction
medium.explanation: The directions identify where each furnishing was to be placed: the lampstand in the south and the table in the north.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the lampstand being in the south and the table in the north?
answers: They were both placed on the same side
They were placed on opposite sides
They were placed outside the Tabernacle
challenge.explanation: South and north are opposite sides, so the lampstand and table stood on different sides.

challenge.question: Which phrase makes clear that the table was not in the Most Holy Place?
challenge.explanation: “Outside the veil” shows that the table was outside the partition leading to the Most Holy Place.

challenge.question: What is the order of information in the verse?
answers: First the table’s location, then the lampstand’s location, and finally the table’s direction
First the table’s direction, then the lampstand’s location, and finally the veil
First the lampstand’s location, then construction of the table, and finally the Tabernacle’s height
challenge.explanation: The verse begins with the table’s location, gives the lampstand’s position opposite it, and ends by specifying the table’s northern location.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the lampstand being in the south and the table in the north?
answers: They were both placed on the same side
They were placed on opposite sides
They were placed outside the Tabernacle
questions.explanation: South and north are opposite sides, so the lampstand and table stood on different sides.

questions.question: Which phrase makes clear that the table was not in the Most Holy Place?
questions.explanation: “Outside the veil” shows that the table was outside the partition leading to the Most Holy Place.

questions.question: What is the order of information in the verse?
answers: First the table’s location, then the lampstand’s location, and finally the table’s direction
First the table’s direction, then the lampstand’s location, and finally the veil
First the lampstand’s location, then construction of the table, and finally the Tabernacle’s height
questions.explanation: The verse begins with the table’s location, gives the lampstand’s position opposite it, and ends by specifying the table’s northern location.

paragraphs.title: The Screen at the Entrance of the Tent

easy.question: What was the screen described in these verses for?
easy.explanation: The verse explicitly says, “thou shalt make an hanging for the door of the tent.”

easy.question: How many pillars supported the screen?
easy.explanation: The text says, “five pillars of shittim wood.”

easy.question: What were the sockets of the pillars made of?
easy.explanation: The final verse says, “five sockets of brass.”

medium.question: What was the relationship between the five pillars and the five sockets?
answers: Each socket was intended for one pillar
The sockets were intended only for the screen
The pillars were intended to cover the Ark
medium.explanation: Since the number of pillars and sockets is the same, each pillar evidently stood in one socket.

medium.question: What is a screen in the phrase “an hanging for the door of the tent”?
answers: A tool for lighting a fire
A cloth curtain or partition closing the entrance
medium.explanation: The context shows that it was a colored fabric curtain at the entrance.

medium.question: What was done to the shittim-wood pillars after they were made?
medium.explanation: The text says, “overlay them with gold.”

challenge.question: What distinguished the screen from the pillars supporting it?
answers: The screen was copper and the pillars were linen
The screen was only gold and the pillars only colored fabric
The screen was colored fabric, and the pillars were wood overlaid with gold
challenge.explanation: The screen was made of blue, purple, scarlet, and fine twined linen, while the pillars were shittim wood overlaid with gold.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the statement that both the pillars and their hooks involved gold?
answers: The pillars and hooks belonged to the same screen-hanging system
The pillars were made entirely of gold
challenge.explanation: The verse mentions the gold-covered pillars and their gold hooks together, showing that both were part of the system for hanging the screen.

challenge.question: What order of actions is described in these verses?
answers: Casting the sockets, weaving the screen, and finally making the pillars
Making the screen, making and overlaying the pillars, and finally casting the sockets
Overlaying the sockets with gold, making the screen, and finally painting the pillars
challenge.explanation: The passage first describes making the screen, then making and overlaying the pillars, and finally casting the copper sockets.

questions.question: What distinguished the screen from the pillars supporting it?
answers: The screen was copper and the pillars were linen
The screen was only gold and the pillars only colored fabric
The screen was colored fabric, and the pillars were wood overlaid with gold
questions.explanation: The screen was made of blue, purple, scarlet, and fine twined linen, while the pillars were shittim wood overlaid with gold.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the statement that both the pillars and their hooks involved gold?
answers: The pillars and hooks belonged to the same screen-hanging system
The pillars were made entirely of gold
questions.explanation: The verse mentions the gold-covered pillars and their gold hooks together, showing that both were part of the system for hanging the screen.

questions.question: What order of actions is described in these verses?
answers: Casting the sockets, weaving the screen, and finally making the pillars
Making the screen, making and overlaying the pillars, and finally casting the sockets
Overlaying the sockets with gold, making the screen, and finally painting the pillars
questions.explanation: The passage first describes making the screen, then making and overlaying the pillars, and finally casting the copper sockets.
